newsitem.title: UK: Thames Water says cutting leaks is priority.
newsitem.headline: Thames Water says cutting leaks is priority.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Thames Water Plc said on Friday that cutting leaks was its top priority, after a newspaper report said the company was trying to avoid tough targets for leakage reduction.
"We are taking (leakage) seriously. It's our top priority but it can't be cured overnight," a spokesman for the company said.
A report in the Guardian newspaper said the company did not want "to be pushed into tough targets by the regulator."
Thames has vowed to halve its leakage by 2005, after around 38 percent of its supplies seeped out of pipes in 1995-96, the spokesman said.
Ofwat, which has warned companies they will face regulatory action if they fail to cut leakage to target levels, wants to see progress when it collates data in July, a spokeswoman said.
She said it was "rubbish" to suggest that Thames' targets were too harsh. "There is nothing wrong with tough targets, as long as they are realistic," she said.
In a report published in November 1996, Ofwat said companies had reported "little reduction in leakage."
It added that "some companies will need to work harder to meet the targets they set for themselves next year (1997-98)."
Leakage became a hot political issue after a drought in 1995, during the country's hottest ever summer, strained supplies and it emerged that over 800 million gallons a day was seeping out of pipes.
Ofwat's options for companies which fail to meet targets include pressing for legislation to impose mandatory leakage targets.
Ofwat expressed its displeasure with Yorkshire Water for its handling of the drought, when it almost had to cut essential domestic supplies, by freezing its prices.
